---
title: "User guide"
description: "How to use tidyvisor at every stage of a study: planning, sample size, the analysis, its assumptions, interpretation and reporting."
---

tidyvisor is a statistical advisor: the chief statistician of a study. You
give it your data and your question, or a fitted result; it gives advice,
the reasons for it and the code to run. This guide explains how to use it
at every stage of a study, and what its advice means.

Each chapter follows the same plan:

1. **The question** the chapter answers, and when it arises.
2. **Code** to copy into R, run on data sets that come with R or with the
   companion packages, so every example works as printed.
3. **The advice** tidyvisor gives, exactly as it prints it.
4. **How to read it**: what each check means, and what the advice does not
   decide for you.

| Chapter | You will learn | Main functions |
|---|---|---|
| [1. Research practice and study design](practice.html) | Good practice at each stage of a study; the unit of replication and pseudoreplication; auditing a data set; reporting guidelines by field | `tv_practice()`, `advise(question = "design")` |
| [2. Power analysis before fieldwork](power.html) | How many samples, traps or sites; effect size, variability and power; nested designs and the intra-class correlation; pilot data | `tv_power()`, `advise(question = "power")` |
| [3. Checking assumptions and choosing the test](assumptions.html) | Normality, equal spread, outliers; t-test, Welch, rank, robust and permutation tests; what to do when assumptions fail | `tidyvisor(data, response, group)`, `tidyvisor(test)` |
| [4. Regression and generalised linear models](regression.html) | Choosing the family from the response; counts, proportions and binary outcomes; effects as rate and odds ratios; diagnostics | `tidyvisor(data, response)`, `tidyvisor(lm/glm)` |
| [5. Mixed, additive and overdispersed models](mixed.html) | Random effects, grouping factors and the intra-class correlation; smooth effects; zero inflation and overdispersion | lme4, mgcv, glmmTMB, aods3 advisors |
| [6. Bayesian models](bayesian.html) | Priors, prior and posterior predictive checks; credible intervals; R-hat, effective sample size and divergences | brms advisor |
| [7. Community and spatial ecology](ecology.html) | Which ordination and which test; gradient length; species distributions, invasions and epidemics | vegan, tidydiversity and tidymapr advisors |
| [8. Writing your own advisor](extending.html) | How the advisors work; registering one for your own package | `register_advisor()`, `advisors()` |

**Where to start.** Planning a study: Chapters 1 and 2. Data in hand:
Chapters 1 and 3, then 4 or 5 for the model. A fitted model whose output
you want explained: pass it to `tidyvisor()` and read the chapter for its
kind of model.

**Worked examples.** The [tutorials](tutorials.html) follow whole studies
from the question to the report.

**The rule behind the advice.** tidyvisor always gives its reasons, so
the advice can be checked and overruled. It knows the statistics; you
know the biology, the design and the question. Where they disagree, the
question wins.

**How to cite.** Run `citation("tidyvisor")` in R.
